title: P-006 installed-PUI engine parity — per-engine real-engine e2e evidence (Claude / Codex / OMP)

scope.subject: Installed PUI binary driving the two shared engine journeys behind the same host and PUI commands, one engine per run.
scope.selection: One journey selected per run by -t filter; the other 15 cases in the file are COLLECTED-NOT-RUN and carry no evidence in that run.
notCovered: Deployed-main verdict: every run below is a local installed-PUI run against the working tree, not :3070.

AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006.requiredEvidence: Run the shared installed-PUI greeting/tool/approval/resume scenario separately for each engine.
AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006.journeyTest: installed PUI with the real <engine> engine > greeting, real file tool, interrupt and continued reply stay in one first-party session

AUTO-BAR-R-03-P-006.requiredEvidence: Run the same scope/tool/mode/carry resume scenario through installed PUI for Claude, Codex and OMP.
AUTO-BAR-R-03-P-006.journeyTest: installed PUI with the real <engine> engine > restores the same native conversation after the operator OS process exits

r10.testName: greeting, real file tool, interrupt and continued reply stay in one first-party session
r10.headNote: The shared tree was swept by git-sync mid-run: the runner banner captured HEAD at run START (5adef9f8e7) while the ledger row records the commit at run END (72dc2e36a6). This is why the runner reported provenance=unknown for this leg. Freshness for the binding is computed from FILE FINGERPRINTS, not commit_sha, so this divergence does not weaken the row.

r03.testName: restores the same native conversation after the operator OS process exits

claude.summary: BOTH claude journeys were re-run over the gateway pool (PUI_REAL_ACCOUNT=auto) and BOTH failed with zero usage-wall hits. r10 exit=1 at 08:34:21Z (FABLE_LIMIT_HITS=0); r03 exit=1 at 08:37:32Z (FABLE_LIMIT_HITS=0). The engine is reached and accepts turns in both, so this is not the account wall and not an instrument problem in the way the earlier reds were. Two independent journeys failing the same way makes a genuine P-006 parity gap more likely than a flake, but the root cause is NOT yet established and no claim is recorded here beyond what was observed.

r10.engineEvidence: Engine process pid 700840 attached; lifecycle starting->ready with reason 'Claude structured stream, SU tools and command executor attached'; owner_turn accepted at 08:31:43.336Z and reported completed at 08:31:44.550Z; nativeSessionId cbc348c5-fc2f-4d38-b0bd-87bcdbe5ca8d.
r10.failureMode: The diagnostics ArrayContaining assertion failed: the session produced 8 frames (lifecycle + command_result only) and NO assistant reply frames. The captured screen shows the owner prompt rendered with an empty reply pane. The owner turn reported 'completed' 1.2s after acceptance without emitting assistant text.
r10.classification: UNRESOLVED — not yet attributed. This is NOT the usage wall (see accountWall below). Candidate causes not yet distinguished: (a) a genuine P-006 parity gap in the Claude engine's assistant-frame emission, (b) the pool account resolved by PUI_REAL_ACCOUNT=auto failing fast in a way the engine swallows into a 'completed' turn. Requires a contrastive probe before any claim is recorded.

codex.blocker: Account out of credits until 2026-09-14T21:26Z (19x HTTP 429). No failover route: PUI_REAL_ACCOUNT accepts only auto|default, and codex identity is a per-session CODEX_HOME rather than an Anthropic-style pooled account, so the gateway pool cannot re-route it.
codex.note: Both P-006 clauses name Claude, Codex AND OMP in requiredEvidence, so codex cannot be silently omitted. Recorded here as explicitly unevidenced rather than absent.

accountWall.claim: The 'You've reached your Fable limit' wall observed on earlier claude legs is specific to the `default` credential and is BYPASSED by routing through the gateway pool.
accountWall.evidence: Earlier leg ts-claude-r03 (account=default) recorded 7 occurrences of 'reached your Fable limit'. Re-run ts2-claude-r10 with PUI_REAL_ACCOUNT=auto over pool accounts recorded FABLE_LIMIT_HITS = 0, and the engine reached lifecycle 'ready' and accepted an owner turn.
accountWall.consequence: Claude real-engine evidence is NOT owner-gated. Only codex remains owner-walled.

retracted: An earlier hypothesis attributed four red legs to a code regression in the range 0db177f606..cff17128f4. WITHDRAWN. The omp reds were caused by the probe script itself passing PUI_REAL_MODEL=papercusp-gateway/claude-sonnet-4-6, a model spec the Agent Chat loop cannot execute; removing that override turned both omp legs green at the same commit. The claude reds were the `default`-account Fable wall. No code regression is implicated.

An earlier note claimed P-006's R-03 clause requires one-to-one causal-pair bindings. WITHDRAWN: that gate is guarded by clause.falsifier.causalPairing === 'one-to-one', and neither P-006 falsifier carries that field (both carry only observation + probeMethod).
instrumentCorrections.tenantStamping: Local test_runs rows carry NULL workspace_id/harness_slug unless PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_HARNESS and PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE_ID are set in the environment BEFORE the run; the binder resolves testRunId tenant-scoped and refuses an unstamped row with test_run_not_found. Both omp rows above were produced with those variables set and carry workspace_id='papercusp-workspace', harness_slug='papercusp'. Filed as EI-22952438885573520.

fingerprints.algorithm: sha256-file-set-v1 — sha256 over JSON.stringify of the deduped, lexically sorted [{path, sha256-of-content}] entry list.

bindings.note: 3420/3421 were bound with adequacy metadata at details.* TOP LEVEL, which the evaluator reads as {} (it reads details.adequacy.* — spec-test-adequacy.ts:317). 3422/3423 re-bind the IDENTICAL facts correctly nested. Bindings are append-only, so the malformed rows remain on the ledger and are superseded, not replaced. Filed as EI-22953893504383574.

adequacyVerdicts.freshnessNote: Both rows evaluate as current ONLY when the evaluator is called with current[] carrying the same source/test fingerprints; omitting current[] yields currentness=unknown and blocks freshness. current[] is an EVALUATOR argument, not a binding property.

integrityCaveat.claim: AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006 reaching verdict:'pass' DOES NOT mean the clause's stated requirement is satisfied.
integrityCaveat.why: The clause's requiredEvidence reads 'Run the shared installed-PUI greeting/tool/approval/resume scenario separately for each engine', and both P-006 clauses name Claude, Codex AND OMP. That requirement is PROSE; there is no machine-readable engine list, so the adequacy evaluator does not enforce per-engine coverage. Demonstrated empirically: binding OMP rows alone moved the clause to verdict:'pass' with wouldBlock:[] while Claude is failing and Codex is unevidenced.
integrityCaveat.consequence: The automated gate is satisfied; the clause is NOT. Do not report P-006 R-10 as met on the strength of this verdict. A grader reading requiredEvidence will and should reject single-engine coverage. The honest status of P-006 is: OMP evidenced, Claude reached-but-failing, Codex blocked.
